NO CABIN YET
Week 6 · Speaking Longer Without Stopping

Long-Haul Flight

A long-haul flight doesn't stop halfway. On the DET Speaking Sample, you read a long question, plan for 30 seconds, and then speak for up to 3 minutes. This week you'll practise planning fast, keeping your "engine" running, and making your answers longer. Every activity has a Fly again button: the second and third tries are where you improve most. You choose your own level. There's no grade, and finishing all the steps counts as attending this week.

~45 min total Choose your level 🎙 Microphone needed Fly again as often as you like A Vocaroo recording
?Not sure what to do? Tap ? How it works at the top of any stop. You will see pictures and easy steps.
Speaking SampleLong prompt, 30 s to plan, up to 3 minutes to speak
Planning fastFind the questions, write keywords, not sentences
FluencyKeep talking with phrases, examples and stories
STOP 01~2 min

Choose Your Cabin

Pick the level that feels right today. Your choice changes the planning time, how long you speak, and your pause goal. Every cabin counts the same for attendance, and you can switch any time.

STOP 02~3 min

Pre-flight Briefing

DET FORMAT · SPEAKING SAMPLE

The Speaking Sample is one of the longest tasks on the DET. Match each part to its description: tap a name, then tap its description. A tip appears for each correct match.

STOP 03~5 min

Flight Plan

DET SKILL · THE 30-SECOND PLAN

DET prompts are long, with 2–3 questions inside. In 30 seconds you need to find the questions and write keywords, not sentences. First tap each question in the prompt to make a plan box. Then put a note card in each box.

TIPA full sentence takes too long to write, and on the test you'll be tempted to read it aloud. Two or three words per box is enough to remind you what to say.
STOP 04~4 min

Keep the Engine Running

DET SKILL · FLUENCY

Everyone gets stuck sometimes. The difference is what you do next. A short English phrase keeps your "engine" running while you think. Silence or restarting makes it stop. Decide: good stall or engine failure?

My 3 engine phrases

Choose 3 phrases you will use in Stops 6 and 7. They'll appear on your dashboard while you speak.

STOP 05~5 min

Stretch It

DET SKILL · MAKING ANSWERS LONGER

A one-line answer lasts about 2 seconds. Add one step at a time: a reason, an example, a detail, a comparison, a wrap-up. Watch the fuel gauge show how long you could speak.

STOP 06~8 min

Altitude Ladder

DET SKILL · SPEAKING STAMINA

Spin for a topic and talk about it three times, a little longer each time. Use the same ideas again and add something new each climb. The topics are short on purpose: this stop builds stamina. The Black Box measures your pauses.

STOP 07~10 min

Full Flight

DET PRACTICE · SPEAKING SAMPLE

Now the real thing: a long DET-style prompt, 30 seconds to plan, then up to 3 minutes of speaking, recorded on Vocaroo (free, no account needed). Paste your link so I can listen and send you feedback.

STOP 08~2 min

Landing Card

This is Week 6's primary assignment. Check your Frequent Flyer Log, add one speaking tip you will use on test day, then copy your summary and paste it into the Week 6 assignment in Classroom. That counts as attending this week.
